chapter_theme: The linga is one and inner; the perfected body (காயசித்தி) comes from the mind's absorption in Brahman and not from any herb; the disciple's questions on dream, the birth of life and the circling of sun and moon are answered with the place called suzhutthi, whose visions and sweetness are a lure to pass. The teacher gives his lineage and denies caste, blames the other siddhas for hiding the egg in cipher, reinterprets the three sandhis as sun, moon and fire, and then, with the purchase of rock salt, turns to alchemy: a red sindhuram that masters the nine metals, oils and a medicine for every disease.
structure_note: The one linga and the breath in Brahman (2376 to 2378); the disciple's question and kaya siddhi, the eight siddhis and the rejection of herbal kalpa (2379 to 2383); the disciple's questions and the suzhutthi (2384 to 2388); the teacher's birth, clan and the denial of caste (2389 to 2392); against the siddhas' cipher, and pooja reread as the three lights (2393 to 2397); the sindhuram and the oils (2397 to 2400).

2376.reading: A litany of the one linga: the linga grown in the central sky and on Mahameru's summit, the linga that is Shakti and the breath, the linga filled in sanchara samadhi, the linga praised by the mind made one through intellect, the linga sprouted in the flower, the linga come to be praised in every direction, the one supreme linga.
2376.nuance: No stone is in the list; every linga named is a state or a place in the body-cosmos, and the eighth line makes them one. பூவரு is unclear, perhaps the lotus of the crown.

2377.reading: Entering the small house called self, fix the breath that has turned its head so that it subsides in Brahman called the king; with mind subdued look closely; the arrow joins the sky; when you eat, son, hunger ends; the coats slip off, and one can be a god even to the gods.
2377.nuance: தலைமாறிப் போன வாசி, the breath that has changed head, is the breath reversed upward, as tradition reads it. பாணம் பாணம் (arrow, arrow) and தேனுக்குந் தேவன் are obscure; the last may be 'a god to the honey' or a corrupt word for the gods.

2378.reading: One can remain through all the yugas in the solitary Brahman; with the mind subdued and silence gained, and yet from great desire within Brahman, the great ones who know the state can take any avatara they wish, as gurus, as kings, as Indra, or as the three gods.
2378.nuance: பேராசை, great desire, is given a positive sense: the one absorbed in Brahman can still choose to appear in the world. The verse grounds the teacher's own serial births (2389, 2390).

2379.reading: The disciple says: my guru Pusundanatha, you said that living things, the whole, and the three murtis are absorbed in Brahman, and then told the sign by which the whole is created again; and you told me to drink the honey; tell me truly its details.
2379.nuance: மது, the honey, is the kalpa of 2341 and 2353, the disciple having rightly heard it as something to be explained rather than taken literally.

2380.reading: He will tell, son Vasinatha: truly when you go into the egg the praised fire enters, and joined with the five senses it becomes awareness; your body becomes very rare without changing, son, a wonder; and when shadow and reflection are lost, the kaya siddhi is firm.
2380.nuance: நிழற்சாய்கை யற்று, losing shadow and reflection, is the traditional mark of the perfected body in Siddhar lore; the verse makes the test physical and observable.

2381.reading: When it has become rare, the eight great siddhis all eight dance; the breath merges and subsides in Brahman; front rank and back rank become one; seeing the silence that bakes and bakes, the place where one stands with the kalai changed is the golden seat; when you see yourself there is no more swimming: the way called samadhi is fixed.
2381.nuance: முன்னணி பின்னணி may be the two breaths or front and back of the body; நீச்சென்றுமில்லை, no swimming, is probably no more crossing the sea of birth; காச்சென்று காச்சிவிடும், the silence that bakes, uses the alchemist's firing for the inner heat. The sense of several words is guessed.

2382.reading: Not knowing the state of tapas they wander disheartened in the world; the great ones who with longing saw silence within thirty years stay young, son; seeing the true guru's feet, worshipping them with compassion, and sending the mind firmly into Brahman, one can be life to life.
2382.nuance: முப்பதுக்குள், within thirty, sets an age for attainment; those who find silence before thirty do not age after it. சீவனுக்குச் சீவன், life of life, is the state and not a metaphor.

2383.reading: One can remain: there is no kalpa of plant or root; in the solitary Brahman, melting, with the mind subdued, as one looks the body itself became firm; not roaming in confusion, not talking sects, not consorting with wastrels, not keeping company with the ... , see the guru's feet and bow deeply.
2383.nuance: செடிபூடு கற்பமில்லை is the plainest rejection of herbal kalpa in the work, and stands against 2353 and the formulas from 2397. கோளர் is unclear (slanderers? the planets?).

2384.reading: The disciple asks the murti of true knowledge to divide and tell the foot and head of the Supreme, to tell firmly the place where dreams are seen in abundance, the place where smell is born, the way the sun and moon circle, and the place where life is born.
2384.nuance: The five questions are answered in 2385 to 2396 with a single place, the suzhutthi; மணம் may be smell or marriage.

2385.reading: He tells with his mouth: at the foot of great Brahman the nerve named before twines unceasingly, and sun and moon circle and dance; the breath stands in the middle without perishing; if the mind goes by that way to the place of suzhutthi, its name is body-suzhutthi; see, and knowing it is awareness.
2385.nuance: சுழுத்தி is the name of the deep-sleep state in the avastha scheme, but here it is a place (சுழுத்தியிடம்) with the qualifier காயான, of the body; the verse seems to mean the sleep-centre where dreams arise, answering 2384. Possibly a confusion with சுழுனை.

2386.reading: There many forms appear and it shows them again like your own deity; like a woman of flesh joining you, as if in intercourse, the suzhutthi that bewitches like honey shows a taste like sweetness; bowing to the guru's grace and knowing the sign, see the state of fullness beyond it.
2386.nuance: Visions of one's deity and erotic dreams are treated alike as the suzhutthi's lure; the teacher does not deny them but ranks them below பூரணம், fullness, and makes the guru's grace the means of passing them.

2387.reading: The unstable ocean became the suzhutthi; join the standing breath to the space; join the chief fire likewise; truly join sun and moon together; without wavering, saying 'one Parapara', with mind subdued look at the crown of the egg: the mind goes to the Supreme without wandering and dances along the sky-street.
2387.nuance: The instruction is a series of joinings, breath, fire, sun and moon, that the tradition reads as the union of the two breaths with the central fire; the plain words are a sequence of 'join' with no measures given.

2388.reading: It dances when, without desire or anger, forgetting mother and kin, one mounts the whole; lock the nine doors and the five senses join in purity; forest or town, what matter, once you see silence; the wish-cow and the wish-tree are yours as siddhi; a lamp set in the house shines, and taken outside it goes to waste.
2388.nuance: நவத்துவாரம், the nine doors, are the body's openings. The lamp image argues against both pilgrimage and display: the practice kept within the body burns, carried out into the world it is lost.

2389.reading: Becoming buddhi and chitta I took the name Pusundan in the world; they call me the son of Vadasali and the son of the rare virgin; among five I was the first born, son; see the vision within the span and the cubit, and they will call that substance Isvara.
2389.nuance: வடசாளி is unexplained. சாண்முழம், a span and a cubit, is the body as the place of vision. The five brothers born of Brahma's seed (2390) are not named elsewhere in the work.

2390.reading: Hear my clan: on earth we five were born from Brahma's seed; I went to the egg of the sky and lived very many crores of years, keeping the mind unfailing in fixity; those who talk are people of the world; see with desire the place reached by letting go and holding.
2390.nuance: The lineage is from Brahma's விந்து, which prepares the claim of 2391 that his only clan is seed. விட்டடைந் தொட்டவிடம் is a riddle phrase: the place reached by releasing and touching.

2391.reading: See, we have no caste or clan; my clan, son, is the clan of seed; one who without seeing talks of caste difference will curl up and perish; in Brahman at the first time all lives were born alike; I too arose that way before, and I sought well the place from which I arose.
2391.nuance: சுக்குலம், the clan of semen, is the argument: all are born the same way from the same stuff, and all lives arose from Brahman together, so caste is a thing said by the unseeing.

2392.reading: A list of faults: not seeking to know the place one arose, not seeing the place one came to in the middle, not seeing the place of birth, reviling the guru, not joining the substance, roaming with the idle, and staying without kinship; the sinner who does not know the Kumbhi and the stone oyster.
2392.nuance: தோஷம் ends seven lines. கும்பி is the hell Kumbhipaka; கற்சிப்பி, the stone oyster, is obscure, perhaps the skull as the shell that holds the pearl.

2393.reading: What jnana has the sinner who does not know? Look at the book Arumugan spoke: it is not said in cipher; look at my valorous book; the siddhas said their books at length but uselessly in concealment, hiding the egg that is the sign and telling it in different ways, which is their fault.
2393.nuance: The charge is against பரிபாஷை, the Siddhars' cipher, by a poet who writes in it; ஆறுமுகன் சொன்ன நூல் is a Murugan-given text he sets beside his own as plain. 2404 then forbids giving his book away, which is concealment by another means.

2394.reading: Without finding fault, going to the egg, seeing the sign of the unspoken mantra, with chitta one, doing pooja to the god at dawn, dusk and noon and gaining clarity; without finding fault, with a loving mind doing tapas facing the guru; when you look with longing and attachment, the supreme Goddess herself comes into your hand.
2394.nuance: அந்திசந்தி யுச்சிக் காலம், the three sandhis, is the Vedic timetable of worship, surprising in a text that scorns pooja; 2395 explains that the three times are the three lights. பற்றாசை, attachment-desire, is for once commended.

2395.reading: If you ask what the dawn, dusk and noon at which she comes are: father, they are the sun, moon and fire become three; go: where the three twine as one and stay is the state of the Brahma-egg; all the lust you have done goes by the grace of Bhuvanai of the trident; and if you join by that way Vani herself dances on your tongue.
2395.nuance: The sandhis are made inner, so the pooja of 2394 is the joining of the three lights; the two gifts are the goddess's removal of past lust and eloquence (Vani on the tongue), which 2396 locates in the uvula.

2396.reading: He tells the house where Vani dwells: along the creeper of the uvula, holding to the egg like a hanging root, the nerve stands fitted in the middle of the stable fire; by that way grace flows, and she speaks in heaven whatever Tamil she pleases.
2396.nuance: Poetic speech is given a bodily seat, the nerve of the uvula; வேணதமிழ், whatever Tamil she wants, makes Tamil the goddess's own tongue.

2397.reading: She speaks all the endless Vedas and Vedic texts, by the Brahman that rose where sruti ends; the great ones who have known themselves win, and do not boast but become silent; who in the world knows the Brahman that has no night or day? Seeing the place where speech ends, be clear; and cunningly buy rock salt, buy it.
2397.nuance: The last line turns without warning from silence to the market: கல்லுப்பு, rock salt, opens the alchemical sequence. Whether this is cipher (salt is a common code for a body-substance) or a literal shopping instruction cannot be settled.

2398.reading: Having bought it, join the brain in the egg and mix in the leaf richly, son; set it inside a twisted spurge, closing the mouth of the hollow and removing the curse; when three months have gone, take out the spurge and, doing no more rite, make a seal of cloth and clay and dry it.
2398.nuance: The verse is an alchemical procedure read here for what it claims: a preparation of salt and some substance sealed in a கள்ளி (spurge) for three months, then sealed with cloth and clay for firing. அண்டத்தில் மூளை (brain in the egg, perhaps an eggshell, perhaps a skull) and வப்பிலை are unclear. சாபந் தீர்த்தே, removing the curse, is the alchemist's word for purifying a substance.

2399.reading: After it has dried, take it, son, and set it devotedly in a kasaputa fire; let it cool, and when you take it out it is a sindhuram of the colour of the dawn sun; smear an atom of it on every drug and set them in the puta: the nine metals yield, and the whole art called vedai is in your hands.
2399.nuance: செந்தூரம் is the red calcined product of Siddha chemistry; நவலோகம் the nine metals; the claim is a universal agent that transmutes. நீருமடா may mean the metals turn to liquid or lose their nature. Read as history of a claim, not as a method.

2400.reading: It is done: all the diseases in the body fly away when an atom of it is eaten; body-siddhi has grown great and one can live joined to the substance; take the oil of the thalaippindam, of the creeper and of the mango; after taking the oil add camphor without hesitation and do pooja to the substance with joy.
2400.nuance: தலைப்பிண்டம் is unexplained (a plant? a prepared ball?); கொடியும் மாவும் may be plant names or a powder. வத்து, the substance, is worshipped, the alchemical product treated as the god, which 2401 continues.

links.note: Both make the linga something other than stone: Tirumular's soul is the Sivalinga in the temple of the heart, Kakapusundar's lingas are the central sky, Meru's summit, Shakti and breath, and samadhi, gathered into one supreme linga.

Arunagirinathar asks not to be the foolish yogi who, thinking impermanent flesh will last, holds the breath and eats herbs in austerity; Kakapusundar promises a body made rare and shadowless, the kaya siddhi, from the fire entering at the crown. The conflict holds if 2380 claims bodily permanence; if the rare body is a figure for freedom from the body, it weakens.

Both tie the eight siddhis to the breath mastered in the central way: Tirumular's come through eightfold yoga when the fire at the root drives the sun and lets the moon drink, Kakapusundar's dance when the breath merges and subsides in Brahman and the body has become rare.

Both promise undimmed youth from the inner practice: Tirumular's breaths set in the upper palate turn grey hair back and make one a child, Kakapusundar's great ones who saw silence before thirty stay young.

2353 tells the disciple to eat the karunelli and the white snake for a deathless head and leg; 2383 says there is no kalpa of plant or root and the body becomes firm only through absorption in Brahman. The conflict is real if 2353 is taken plainly; the tradition escapes it by reading its herb and snake as cipher for inner substances, which 2383 would then be stating openly.

Both displace the kalpa herb with an inner act: Tirumular says praising the Lord night and morning makes the body as if transmuted by the herb, Kakapusundar that the body grows firm in Brahman and no plant or root kalpa exists.

Both deny caste to the knower: for Tirumular those who set Nandi in love by knowledge have no caste, no stain and no pride; Kakapusundar's only clan is seed, all lives having arisen alike from Brahman.

The Naladiyar says good caste and bad caste are empty words and lineage is made by tapas, learning and effort; Kakapusundar says caste is spoken only by the unseeing and all are born of the same seed. Both empty birth-caste, though the Naladiyar puts conduct in its place and Kakapusundar puts common origin.

2348 scorns those who set up a linga, bathe it and offer flowers; 2394 prescribes pooja to the god at the three sandhis with the chitta one. 2395 shows the sandhis are the three lights, so the pooja kept is inner and the rejection of 2348 is of the outer act only.
2394 prescribes pooja at dawn, dusk and noon; 2395 defines those three times as sun, moon and fire twined as one at the crown, turning the ritual timetable into the practice of the lights.

source_issues: 2377: பாணம் பாணம் and தேனுக்குந் தேவனா are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2385 to 2387: சுழுத்தி is used for a body-place, where the rest of the work has சுழுனை (sushumna); either a different term or a scribal confusion.
2398: வப்பிலையும் is unclear, perhaps அப்பிலையும்; தமர்வாய் is uncertain.
2400: தலைப்பிண்டம், கொடி and மா are unidentified substances.
